Table 3. HERA single-epoch data product and preprocessing summary.

ItemValueNotes
Instrument / dateHERA, 2022-04-03single-epoch snapshots
Data sourceMesarcik et al. (2022), ZenodoDOI: 10.5281/zenodo.6724065
Observation window$ \sim $19:42-20:42 UTCfrom Zenodo metadata
Data formatPython pickle (list of 4 arrays)loaded via pd.read.pickle
Array 0 shape(420, 512, 512, 1) float16visibility amplitude
Array 1 shape(420, 512, 512, 1) boolAOFlagger mask
Number of snapshots $ N_{ ext{snap}} $420first axis of array 0
Per-snapshot matrix size$ T = 420, F = 512 $time samples $ imes $ frequency channels
Frequency span50-225 MHzstated analysis band
Channel spacing $ \Delta u $0.341796875 MHzmeasured from frequency axis
Time resolution $ \Delta t $1.0 sverified from metadata/header
Snapshot duration $ T_{ ext{snap}} $420 s$ T_{ ext{snap}} = T imes \Delta t $
BaselineBaseline index 0fixed per snapshot
PolarizationXXfixed
Input quantity$ |V(t, u)| $amplitude of calibrated visibility
Normalizationmedian-MADapplied to form $ D \in \mathbb{R}^{T imes F} $
RFI maskAOFlagger boolean maskseparate array (not NaNs)
Flagged fractionmean 2.75%, median 2.24%10/90%: 1.13/5.88%
Science core (protected)140-160 MHzredshifted 21 cm at $ z \approx 7.9-9.1 $
Science band (evaluation)130-170 MHzcore $ \pm $10 MHz
Injection example150 MHz, amp = 0.4, $ \sigma_{ u} = 0.5 $ MHzrank-2 proxy validation

The protected EoR window of 140–160 MHz corresponds to the redshifted 21 cm line at  $ z \approx 7.9–9.1 $, consistent with the frequency range commonly targeted by HERA foreground-avoidance analyses (e.g., DeBoer et al. 2017; Abdurashidova et al. 2022).
